```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 3.6, out.width = "100%")
library(ggplot2)

BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; ORANGE <- "#eb6834"

gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0])))

theme_bench <- function()
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.015, 0.985),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key = element_blank())

log2_axis <- function(breaks, suffix = "", ...)
  list(transform = "log2", breaks = breaks, labels = paste0(breaks, suffix), ...)

# PEtab models by first author and year, classical problems marked with a dagger
label <- function(problem) {
  classic <- c(VanDerPol_mu1000 = "van der Pol", OREGO = "OREGO", Robertson = "Robertson",
               E5 = "E5", HIRES = "HIRES", Pollution = "Pollution",
               Brusselator1D_N24 = "Brusselator, N = 24", Brusselator1D_N64 = "Brusselator, N = 64",
               FitzHughNagumo_N24 = "FitzHugh-Nagumo, N = 24",
               FitzHughNagumo_N64 = "FitzHugh-Nagumo, N = 64")
  out <- sub("^([A-Za-z]+)_.*?([0-9]{4})$", "\\1 \\2", problem, perl = TRUE)
  out <- sub("^Brannmark", "Brännmark", sub("^Raimundez", "Raimúndez",
             sub("^SalazarCavazos", "Salazar-Cavazos", out)))
  hit <- problem %in% names(classic)
  out[hit] <- paste0(classic[problem[hit]], "†")
  out
}

d <- read.csv("bench/results.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ok   <- d[d$ok, ]
auto <- ok[ok$pinned == "auto", ]

# plain solves per problem, backend and tolerance: the unit of the derivative costs
plain <- auto[auto$mode == "nosens", c("problem", "backend", "rtol", "time_ms")]
names(plain)[4] <- "t_plain"
```

Both backends take the right-hand side, Jacobian, events and
linear-solver choice from the same expression graph and run at the same
tolerances, so a head-to-head measurement compares the numerical cores.
The figures and tables below are drawn from the saved results of one run,
`vignettes/articles/bench/` in the repository; nothing is measured when
the site is built. The suite itself is in
[`benchmarks/`](https://github.com/dModverse/cppDE/tree/master/benchmarks),
whose README describes its options, the problem tiers and how to run it
on a cluster.

## Setup

The suite comprises $43$ problems (table below): $33$ published
systems-biology models of the PEtab benchmark collection
[@hass2019benchmark; @schmiester2021petab] and $10$ classical test
problems, with $n_x = 2$ to $504$ states. First-order sensitivities run
forward for up to $M = 32$ parameters and in reverse on the two models
with $M \ge 120$, Lang and Chen. Both backends use BDF/NDF with the
automatically selected linear solver at
$(\mathrm{rtol}, \mathrm{atol}) \in \{(10^{-4}, 10^{-6}),
(10^{-7}, 10^{-9}), (10^{-10}, 10^{-12})\}$, and a cell reports the
median of five batches of at least $0.25$ s. The suite ran on AMD EPYC
7513 nodes with twelve workers each; both backends of a cell ran in the
same worker. Ratios are geometric means over the three tolerances.

Both backends also share the output grid and the initial values, and
neither calls back into R during the solve. Sensitivities come from
forward automatic differentiation in `cppODE()` and from the CVODES
forward sensitivity equations in `cvode()`. The PEtab models are read from their SBML. A switch in time
inside the simulated window becomes a time-triggered event, and a
parameter that sets a switching time is left out of the sensitivities.
The differentiated parameters are those PEtab estimates that enter the
ODE, at most $32$ for the forward runs; the initial values are fixed
unless the model estimates them. Pre-equilibration conditions are not
applied: every trajectory starts from the initial values of the SBML
model, for both backends.

```{r problems}
pr <- unique(auto[auto$backend == "cppde" & auto$mode == "sens1",
                  c("problem", "nstates", "nsens")])
pr <- pr[order(pr$nstates, tolower(pr$problem)), ]
tab <- data.frame(problem = label(pr$problem), nx = pr$nstates, M = pr$nsens)
blocks <- split(tab, rep(1:3, each = ceiling(nrow(tab) / 3))[seq_len(nrow(tab))])
blocks <- lapply(blocks, function(b) b[seq_len(max(sapply(blocks, nrow))), ])
wide <- do.call(cbind, unname(blocks))
wide[is.na(wide)] <- ""
names(wide) <- rep(c("problem", "$n_x$", "$M$"), 3)
knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE, align = rep(c("l", "r", "r"), 3),
             caption = paste("Benchmark problems with their numbers of states $n_x$ and",
                             "differentiated parameters $M$. PEtab models are named by first",
                             "author and year; † marks the classical test problems, van der",
                             "Pol at $\\mu = 1000$ and the one-dimensional Brusselator and",
                             "FitzHugh-Nagumo systems on $N$ grid points."))
```

## Head to head

```{r speedup, fig.cap = "Head-to-head ratio of the two backends, one marker per problem and mode; above the line `cppODE()` is faster. The plain solve is placed at the $M$ of its sensitivity counterpart."}
LABELS <- c(nosens = "without sensitivities", sens1 = "with sensitivities")
hh  <- auto[auto$mode %in% c("nosens", "sens1") & auto$deriv %in% c("none", "forward"), ]
key <- c("problem", "mode", "rtol", "nstates")
m   <- merge(hh[hh$backend == "cppde", c(key, "nsens", "time_ms")],
             hh[hh$backend == "cvode", c(key, "time_ms")],
             by = key, suffixes = c(".cp", ".cv"))
m$ratio <- m$time_ms.cv / m$time_ms.cp

# one point per problem and mode, the geometric mean over the tolerances
pp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(m, list(m$problem, m$mode), drop = TRUE),
  function(g) data.frame(problem = g$problem[1], mode = g$mode[1],
                         M = g$nsens[1], ratio = gm(g$ratio))))
Mof  <- setNames(pp$M[pp$mode == "sens1"], pp$problem[pp$mode == "sens1"])
pp$M <- unname(Mof[pp$problem])
pp   <- pp[is.finite(pp$M) & pp$M > 0, ]
pp$mode <- factor(pp$mode, levels = names(LABELS))

ggplot(pp, aes(M, ratio, colour = mode, shape = mode)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(size = 2, stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(0.71, 1, 1.41, 2, 2.83), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(nosens = BLUE, sens1 = ORANGE), labels = LABELS,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(nosens = 1, sens1 = 2), labels = LABELS, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = expression(italic(t)["cvode()"] / italic(t)["cppODE()"])) +
  theme_bench()
```

**Plain solves.** `cppODE()` is faster on $41$ of $43$
problems, by a geometric mean of $1.15$, with about as many steps as
CVODE (ratios of accepted steps and right-hand-side evaluations $1.02$
and $1.06$). The margin is a cost per step: the model functions are
inlined into the stepper, whereas CVODE calls them through function
pointers and dispatches every vector operation through the
`N_Vector` table.

**Forward sensitivities.** `cppODE()` is faster on $34$ of
$41$ problems, by $1.29$, and the ratio grows with $M$: $1.01$ for
$M \le 3$, $1.22$ for $4 \le M \le 12$ and $1.52$ for
$13 \le M \le 32$. CVODES evaluates one Jacobian-vector product per
parameter; the in-tree backend evaluates $f$ once on a dual state that
holds all $M$ tangents and needs about one eleventh of the
right-hand-side evaluations. The dual evaluation has a cost per state
component independent of $M$, so problems with few parameters fall
below parity: six of the seven slower ones have $M \le 6$, the lowest
being Salazar-Cavazos ($n_x = 75$, $M = 6$) at $0.67$.

## Gradients

```{r gradient, fig.cap = "Cost of one gradient by forward sensitivities in units of the plain solve of the same problem and backend, with least-squares lines."}
g <- merge(auto[auto$mode == "sens1" & auto$deriv == "forward",
                c("problem", "backend", "rtol", "nsens", "time_ms")],
           plain, by = c("problem", "backend", "rtol"))
g$cost <- g$time_ms / g$t_plain
g <- aggregate(cost ~ problem + backend + nsens, data = g, FUN = gm)
GLAB <- c(cppde = "cppODE()", cvode = "cvode()")

# the forward cost is linear in M: one least-squares line per backend
fit_line <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(GLAB), function(b) {
  f <- lm(cost ~ nsens, data = g[g$backend == b, ])
  M <- exp(seq(log(1), log(max(g$nsens)), length.out = 200))
  data.frame(backend = b, M = M, cost = predict(f, data.frame(nsens = M)))
}))

ggplot(g, aes(nsens, cost, colour = backend)) +
  geom_line(data = fit_line, aes(M, cost), linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = backend), size = 2, stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = GLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = GLAB, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = "gradient cost / plain solve") +
  theme_bench()
```

Measured in plain solves, the cost of one gradient by forward
sensitivities is linear in $M$: $1.8 + 0.60\,M$ for `cppODE()` and
$1.2 + 0.84\,M$ for CVODES, about $92$ and $129$ at $M = 152$. The
[discrete adjoint](methods-reverse.html) costs $6.3$ plain solves on
Chen and $3.6$ on Lang, independent of $M$. The
[CVODES adjoint](methods-cvode.html#asa), measured on Lang, costs $27$
plain CVODE solves and takes $8.8$ to $13.7$ times as long as the
discrete adjoint.

```{r adjoint, fig.height = 2.8, fig.cap = "Time of one gradient by the CVODES adjoint over the time by the discrete adjoint, per model and tolerance; right of the line the discrete adjoint is faster."}
a  <- read.csv("bench/adjoint.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
a  <- a[a$ok, ]
aw <- merge(a[a$backend == "cppde", c("problem", "rtol", "nsens", "nstates", "time_ms")],
            a[a$backend == "cvode", c("problem", "rtol", "time_ms")],
            by = c("problem", "rtol"), suffixes = c(".cp", ".cv"))
aw$ratio <- aw$time_ms.cv / aw$time_ms.cp
lab <- unique(a[a$backend == "cppde" & a$problem %in% aw$problem,
                c("problem", "nsens", "nstates")])
lab$label <- sprintf("%s  (M = %d, n = %d)", sub(" [0-9]{4}$", "", label(lab$problem)),
                     lab$nsens, lab$nstates)
lab <- lab[order(lab$nsens), ]
aw$label <- factor(lab$label[match(aw$problem, lab$problem)], levels = lab$label)
aw$rtol  <- factor(format(aw$rtol, scientific = TRUE),
                   levels = format(sort(unique(aw$rtol), decreasing = TRUE),
                                   scientific = TRUE))
RCOL <- setNames(c("#9ec5f3", "#2a78d6", "#0d3b73"), levels(aw$rtol))

ggplot(aw, aes(ratio, label, colour = rtol, shape = rtol)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, stroke = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = RCOL, name = "rtol") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 2, 0), name = "rtol") +
  labs(x = expression(italic(t)["CVODES adjoint"] / italic(t)["discrete adjoint"]),
       y = NULL) +
  theme_bench() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.position.inside = NULL)
```

A separate run on the six models with $M \ge 40$, one core per model,
compares the two adjoints on the four of them with a CVODES result. The
CVODES adjoint takes $8.7$ to $18.8$ times as long on Lang,
Lucarelli and Raimúndez, and $1.0$ to $1.5$
times on Zheng ($n_x = 15$), where a solve takes about a
millisecond. The discrete adjoint runs backward over the steps of the
forward solve, whereas CVODES chooses its own backward steps and
recomputes the forward state between checkpoints. At
$\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$ both gradients deviate from the reference by
$10^{-10}$ to $5 \cdot 10^{-7}$.

## Second order

```{r hessian, fig.cap = "Cost of one Hessian of the summed outputs in units of the plain solve. The lines are power laws fitted in log-log over $M > 1$."}
h <- merge(ok[ok$mode == "sens2", c("problem", "rtol", "deriv", "nsens", "time_ms")],
           plain[plain$backend == "cppde", c("problem", "rtol", "t_plain")],
           by = c("problem", "rtol"))
h$cost <- h$time_ms / h$t_plain
h <- aggregate(cost ~ problem + deriv + nsens, data = h, FUN = gm)
HLAB <- c(`forward-forward` = "forward over forward",
          `forward-reverse` = "forward over reverse")
h$deriv <- factor(h$deriv, levels = names(HLAB))

# power laws fitted in log-log over M > 1, one per mode
pl_line <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(HLAB), function(dm) {
  s <- h[h$deriv == dm & h$nsens > 1, ]
  f <- lm(log(cost) ~ log(nsens), data = s)
  M <- exp(seq(log(1), log(max(s$nsens)), length.out = 100))
  data.frame(deriv = dm, M = M, cost = exp(predict(f, data.frame(nsens = M))),
             slope = coef(f)[2])
}))
pl_line$deriv <- factor(pl_line$deriv, levels = names(HLAB))
slopes <- tapply(pl_line$slope, pl_line$deriv, `[`, 1)
HLAB2 <- setNames(sprintf("%s, slope %.1f", HLAB, slopes[names(HLAB)]), names(HLAB))

ggplot(h, aes(nsens, cost, colour = deriv)) +
  geom_line(data = pl_line, aes(M, cost), linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = deriv), size = 2, stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`forward-forward` = BLUE, `forward-reverse` = ORANGE),
                      labels = HLAB2, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`forward-forward` = 1, `forward-reverse` = 2),
                     labels = HLAB2, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("differentiated parameters" ~ italic(M)),
       y = "Hessian cost / plain solve") +
  theme_bench()
```

The Hessian of the summed outputs is measured for `cppODE()` alone, on
models with at most $30$ states:
[forward over reverse](methods-forward-reverse.html) with up to $32$
directions, forward over forward up to $10$ states and $10$ directions.
Fitted in log-log, the cost grows with exponent $1.9$ forward over
forward and $0.6$ forward over reverse. The two break even at $M = 3$;
forward over reverse is $3.0$ times faster at $M = 6$ and $9$ to $14$
times at $M = 9$ and $10$. At $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$ the Hessians
deviate from the forward-over-forward Hessian at the reference tolerance
by a median of $8.1 \cdot 10^{-10}$ (forward over forward) and
$1.8 \cdot 10^{-8}$ (forward over reverse).

## Linear solver

```{r sparse, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.4, out.width = "65%", fig.cap = "Gain of the sparse over the dense linear solver, one marker per model and backend."}
sw <- ok[ok$pinned != "auto" & ok$mode %in% c("nosens", "sens1") &
         ok$deriv %in% c("none", "forward"), ]
sg <- merge(sw[sw$pinned == "dense",  c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol", "nstates", "time_ms")],
            sw[sw$pinned == "sparse", c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol", "time_ms")],
            by = c("problem", "backend", "mode", "rtol"), suffixes = c(".d", ".s"))
sg$gain <- sg$time_ms.d / sg$time_ms.s
sg <- aggregate(gain ~ problem + backend + nstates, data = sg, FUN = gm)
SLAB <- c(cppde = "cppODE()", cvode = "cvode()")

ggplot(sg, aes(nstates, gain, colour = backend, shape = backend)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(size = 2, stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  do.call(scale_x_continuous, log2_axis(c(8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512),
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  do.call(scale_y_continuous, log2_axis(c(1, 1.41, 2, 2.83, 4), "×",
                                        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = SLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = SLAB, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("states" ~ italic(n)[x]),
       y = expression(italic(t)["dense"] / italic(t)["sparse"])) +
  theme_bench()
```

Seventeen models were solved again with the linear solver pinned to
dense and to sparse. The sparse gain is the same for both backends and
grows from $1.09$ at $n_x = 8$ to $3.3$ at $n_x = 504$; the automatic
selection chose the sparse path in every case.

## Accuracy

Against a reference at $\mathrm{atol} = 10^{-14}$,
$\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-12}$ the error of `cppODE()` is a median
$0.99$ times that of CVODE without sensitivities (central $90\,\%$ of
the problems between $0.51$ and $1.51$) and $1.09$ with sensitivities
(between $0.66$ and $2.37$). The reference is itself a CVODE solution,
which favours CVODE. The error of a solve is the largest deviation of a
state from the reference, divided by the largest value that state takes
along the reference trajectory.

```{r work-precision, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 12, fig.cap = "Work-precision of the plain solves, one panel per problem: scaled error against time per solve at the three tolerances; down and to the left is better."}
wp <- auto[auto$mode == "nosens" & is.finite(auto$err) & auto$err > 0,
           c("problem", "nstates", "backend", "rtol", "time_ms", "err")]
lev <-unique(wp[order(wp$nstates, tolower(wp$problem)), "problem"])
wp$panel <- factor(label(wp$problem), levels = label(lev))
wp <- wp[order(wp$problem, wp$backend, wp$rtol), ]

ggplot(wp, aes(time_ms, err, colour = backend, shape = backend)) +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10(guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_log()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(cppde = BLUE, cvode = ORANGE), labels = SLAB,
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(cppde = 1, cvode = 2), labels = SLAB, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 6, labeller = label_wrap_gen(18)) +
  labs(x = "time per solve [ms]", y = "scaled error") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top",
        strip.background = element_blank())
```

## Failures

Six of the $1083$ cells failed, all at $\mathrm{rtol} = 10^{-10}$: the
forward sensitivities of `cppODE()` on Oliveira with each linear solver
and on Weber, and forward over forward on the same two models.

## Running the suite

The suite needs the PEtab collection, fetched once, and runs in three
tiers of increasing coverage; a full run of all modes takes hours and is
meant for an idle machine or a cluster:

```sh
Rscript benchmarks/fetch-models.R
Rscript benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R --tier full --modes nosens,sens1,sens2
```

Each run writes `results.csv`, a README with the configuration and the
tables, and its figures to `benchmarks/results/<timestamp>/`.
